items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.summary: Navalia is a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents by incorporating verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training. It uses corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct computation chains for generating analytical tasks with traceable dependencies. Independent LLM review and programmatic checks are employed to verify evidence consistency and answer accuracy. These verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to enhance long-horizon execution. The method consistently improves evidence integration, tool use, and task execution across various benchmarks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training" details a framework for advancing Cowork Agents using verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training. The methodology involves using corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct computation chains for generating analytical tasks with traceable dependencies. Independent large language model review and programmatic checks are utilized to verify evidence consistency and answer accuracy. These verified tasks subsequently feed into trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to improve long-horizon execution. This process consistently yields improvements in evidence integration, tool use, and task execution across various benchmarks. The research indicates a pathway for creating more reliable and capable autonomous agents in complex reasoning environments.

items.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
items.summary: Large language models enable agents to perform autonomous planning and execution for smart manufacturing tasks. Challenges in this field stem from dynamic environments, physical constraints, and reliability demands in industrial settings. The paper systematically analyzes industrial agents, proposing a taxonomy and a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop execution. It details core modules and operational mechanisms for these agents. Finally, the work reviews applications across the industrial lifecycle and suggests future research directions.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing" details the development of large language model driven agents for autonomous planning and execution in smart manufacturing tasks. The research systematically analyzes industrial agents and proposes a taxonomy and a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop execution. This framework details core modules and operational mechanisms designed to address the challenges presented by dynamic environments and physical constraints in industrial settings. The work outlines applications across the industrial lifecycle and suggests future research directions. This development points toward the implementation of sophisticated autonomous systems within complex industrial operations.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.summary: The research proposes a method using multi-objective reinforcement learning with Large Language Models for Pareto-optimal Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation. Existing methods struggle to generate diverse solutions across multiple trade-offs like Power, Performance, and Area simultaneously. The proposed method trains a generation pipeline to optimize the coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set. A reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) is used to measure a generated circuit's contribution to the Pareto front. Evaluations show the method significantly improves Hypervolume and circuit diversity compared to baseline methods.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models" details a method employing multi-objective reinforcement learning with large language models for generating Register-Transfer Level code that optimizes trade-offs between power, performance, and area. The research addresses the difficulty existing methods have in producing diverse solutions across these multiple constraints simultaneously. The proposed method trains a generation pipeline to maximize the coverage improvement across the entire Pareto solution set. A reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution is utilized to quantify the generated circuit's impact on the Pareto front. Evaluations indicate that this approach significantly enhances Hypervolume and circuit diversity when compared to baseline methods. This advancement suggests a new avenue for more efficient and comprehensive hardware design automation.

items.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
items.summary: Automated theorem provers in Lean often discard valuable error information during failed steps when using pure sampling. This work introduces a bounded, online repair module that samples tactics and repairs failed tactics based on the compiler's error messages. A pretrained repair model is used to fix individual rejected steps in place, rather than discarding them. This method improves the solve rate by up to 32% compared to sampling-only baselines. The repair strategy is most effective for shallow tactic-execution failures, yielding significant gains with predictable runtime trade-offs.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4" reports on a method for improving automated theorem proving in Lean 4 by introducing a bounded, online repair module. This work demonstrates that using a repair mechanism based on compiler error messages, rather than pure sampling, increases the solve rate by up to thirty-two percent compared to sampling-only baselines. The methodology involves employing a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps directly within the theorem proving process. This technique operates by sampling tactics and subsequently repairing failed tactics based on the specific error messages provided by the compiler, ensuring that error information is not discarded. The repair strategy proves most effective for failures occurring during shallow tactic execution, resulting in substantial gains with manageable runtime trade-offs. This advancement suggests a pathway toward more robust and efficient automated reasoning systems in the field of formal verification.

items.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
items.summary: Conversational recommendation systems using vision-language models face challenges in scaling to multiple product domains. LightCRS is a lightweight framework that unifies multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It precomputes multimodal product representations offline and uses a compact, query-conditioned cross-attention module for online inference. The system achieves state-of-the-art performance on a 25-domain benchmark, significantly improving metrics while reducing query latency. This approach enhances performance by jointly training across domains and optimizing the inference process.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System" reports on a new framework for conversational recommendation systems that addresses scaling challenges across multiple product domains by unifying multimodal conversational recommendation. The system achieves state-of-the-art performance on a twenty-five-domain benchmark while reducing query latency. The LightCRS framework is a lightweight method that unifies multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation by precomputing multimodal product representations offline and employing a compact, query-conditioned cross-attention module for online inference. This approach is accomplished by jointly training across domains and optimizing the inference process to enhance performance. This advancement suggests a path toward more efficient and scalable conversational AI systems in complex product recommendation scenarios.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.summary: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable, modality-aware agentic AI framework designed for structuring radiology reports. It generates structured reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands without requiring external APIs or internet connectivity. The system is built using a Small Language Model and operates with low resource requirements, running on standard laptop CPUs. It supports four modalities, including Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. The workflow involves concept extraction, ontology grounding, and structured report generation, culminating in a human-in-the-loop correction phase.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring" details an agentic AI framework designed for structuring radiology reports with edge deployment capabilities. The system successfully generates structured reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands without reliance on external APIs or internet connectivity. The methodology involves utilizing a Small Language Model to perform concept extraction and ontology grounding across four modalities including Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. This process facilitates structured report generation through a workflow incorporating human-in-the-loop correction. This advancement demonstrates the feasibility of deploying complex language processing tasks directly on standard laptop CPUs for specialized medical documentation. Future developments in on-device multimodal AI are anticipated.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.summary: DataPraxis is a framework designed to scale analytics tasks by evolving workspaces with verified findings and artifacts. It progressively enriches workspaces and inherits these to uncover deeper questions, constructing tasks from accumulated, verified findings and their dependencies. The framework verifies analytical results during evolution and after task assembly. This process leads to the creation of the DataPraxis-5K dataset, which is used to train large models like DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B. These models achieve competitive performance on established benchmarks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution" details a framework designed to scale analytics tasks by evolving workspaces with verified findings and artifacts, leading to the creation of large language models trained on the resulting dataset. The framework operates by progressively enriching workspaces with verified findings, allowing the system to inherit these results to uncover deeper questions and construct tasks based on accumulated, verified findings and their dependencies. Analytical results are verified during the evolution process and after task assembly, a methodology that culminated in the DataPraxis-5K dataset. This dataset is subsequently used to train large models such as DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B, which demonstrate competitive performance on established benchmarks. This advancement indicates a method for systematically building complex analytical knowledge from verified data. Further research is anticipated in scaling these verified workspace evolution techniques.

items.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates
items.summary: A method combining a large language model and reinforcement learning is proposed for autonomous construction and progress updates. An enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm plans actions for a mobile crane based on construction tasks. Robot kinematics and control algorithms ensure the generated actions are executable by the crane. A customized embedding model extracts relevant information from the construction environment based on user interests. A large language model, such as ChatGPT 5, is then utilized to update progress, provide safety information, and generate reports, with feasibility verified through construction experiments.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates" reports on a method combining a large language model and reinforcement learning for autonomous construction and progress updates. An enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to plan actions for a mobile crane based on construction tasks, with robot kinematics and control algorithms ensuring the generated actions are executable. A customized embedding model extracts relevant information from the construction environment based on user interests, and a large language model is then utilized to update progress, provide safety information, and generate reports, with feasibility verified through construction experiments. This research demonstrates the integration of advanced machine learning techniques to facilitate autonomous construction management. Further development in this area indicates increased potential for intelligent automation in the construction sector.

items.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
items.summary: Large language models struggle with classical planning, but current benchmarks do not effectively separate structural complexity from semantic interpretability. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ significantly outperforms other learned predictors for estimating structural difficulty. Renaming predicates demonstrates that LLM planning success degrades as the semantic complexity increases, while conditioning information predicts difficulty better than trained models. Hybrid planning relies more on calibrating to LLM outcomes than on structural scores. Therefore, improving hybrid planning should focus on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability" reports on the challenges large language models face with classical planning problems and introduces a method for separating structural complexity from semantic interpretability. The research demonstrates that the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic h add significantly outperforms other learned predictors for estimating structural difficulty in planning tasks. The study found that renaming predicates resulted in degraded LLM planning success as semantic complexity increased, and that conditioning information proved more effective at predicting difficulty than models trained without explicit semantic awareness. Hybrid planning approaches are shown to rely more on calibrating to observed LLM outcomes than on purely structural scores. Improving hybrid planning necessitates focusing on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics. This research directs future efforts toward building models that explicitly account for the semantic meaning embedded within planning problems.

items.title: Expert-Guided Rubrics as Dense Reward Signals for Reinforcement Learning in Non-Verifiable Domains
items.summary: Large language models deployed in non-verifiable domains require assessment beyond simple binary rewards from reinforcement learning. Subject-matter expert (SME) judgment, which is graded, can be converted into dense reward signals. The method combines this SME judgment with retrieval-based metrics to create a hybrid training signal. This approach addresses the issue where sparse rewards fail to provide useful learning signals in such settings. Experiments demonstrated up to 6% improvement in retrieval metrics compared to sparse-reward baselines.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Expert-Guided Rubrics as Dense Reward Signals for Reinforcement Learning in Non-Verifiable Domains" details a method for improving reinforcement learning in complex settings by utilizing expert judgment as dense reward signals. The research combines subject-matter expert grading with retrieval-based metrics to generate a hybrid training signal. Experiments showed an improvement of up to six percent in retrieval metrics when compared to baselines relying solely on sparse rewards. This approach addresses the limitations encountered when deploying large language models in domains where simple binary rewards are insufficient for effective learning. The methodology involves integrating human expert assessments with information retrieval scores to create richer feedback for the learning process. This advancement suggests a path toward more robust training for artificial intelligence systems operating outside clearly defined, verifiable environments.

items.title: CoASFL: Coupled Consistency Optimization for Asynchronous Split Federated Learning
items.summary: Split Federated Learning (SFL) suffers from horizontal and vertical inconsistencies, leading to model divergence and client drift in asynchronous settings. CoASFL proposes a framework to address these issues by incorporating dynamic activation merging and a consistency-aware model aggregation mechanism. It ensures more consistent activation sequences from heterogeneous clients to reduce horizontal inconsistency. Furthermore, it dynamically adjusts aggregation weights based on client participation to mitigate vertical inconsistency. Experiments on an 80-device testbed show CoASFL significantly outperforms other SFL approaches in terms of speed and accuracy.

items.title: Beyond Scalar Leaderboards: Adaptive Sampling for Pareto Frontier Identification in Multi-Objective LLM Arenas
items.summary: Evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) requires multi-objective assessment across various performance dimensions. The paper introduces Vector-Borda Empirical-Gap Elimination (VB-EGE), an adaptive sampling algorithm for efficiently finding models on the Pareto frontier in arena-style evaluations. VB-EGE progressively removes models once sufficient statistical evidence confirms their Pareto status. The method operates under a multi-objective Bradley-Terry model and provides instance-dependent bounds on sample complexity. Experiments on real-world datasets confirm VB-EGE's empirical effectiveness.

items.title: Dynamic Dual-Feedback Conformal Inference for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Uncertainty quantification in time series forecasting is challenging due to temporal dependence and distributional shifts. Dynamic Dual-feedback Conformal Inference (DDCI) is proposed to address this by incorporating a dual-feedback mechanism. This mechanism uses both actual feedback from true observations and estimated feedback from conformal inference to adjust prediction intervals. Actual feedback drives the primary interval adjustment, while estimated feedback moderates expansions or contractions using empirical thresholds. DDCI results in more stable and narrower prediction intervals while maintaining practical coverage.

items.title: Steerable Pluralistic Policy Alignment from Anonymized Crowd Feedback
items.summary: A novel framework called Preference-PCA Pluralistic Learning (P3L) is proposed for pluralistic alignment using anonymized crowd feedback. This method learns trajectory embeddings and a shared basis of preference directions via PCA decomposition without needing annotator identities. The approach enables rapid and accurate personalized reward learning and policy optimization at test time. Experiments show that P3L facilitates steerable personal alignment that generalizes to new users and achieves competitive performance. Furthermore, the method reduces computational cost while supporting variable adaptation query budgets.

items.title: What Moved the Alarm Score? Causal Attribution with Exact Computation and Scarce-Incident Estimation
items.summary: Alarms in industrial systems require explanations tracing changes in the data-generating process to the alarm score, despite scarce incident data. The paper formulates the alarm-score change as a Shapley game over hybrid structural causal model (SCM) states to attribute propagation. It distinguishes between changes in structural functions and exogenous laws for a finer-grained report of influence. Exact Shapley vectors are computed in polynomial time for linear SCMs and quadratic scores using first- and second-moment recursion. The method adapts a reference SCM to estimate these changes from limited data, providing attribution-error bounds.

items.title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD) addresses challenges in multi-teacher on-policy distillation by incorporating student capabilities into supervision allocation. It merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization before guiding distillation. CA-MOPD uses verifier-estimated teacher-student capability gaps to dynamically adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision is reduced when capability gaps close and increased when student capability regresses, while retaining dense token-level guidance. Across six benchmarks, CA-MOPD outperformed other methods, showing significant gains over naive MOPD and Open-MOPD.

items.title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
items.summary: Latent world models allow agents to plan in latent space by minimizing the $\ell_2$ distance to a goal latent. The noise in the latent space is structured by a regularizer that promotes variance in signal-less directions. Fitting the state dynamics model $A$ yields the covariance, and its eigenbasis provides a stable basis for planning cost. Restricting the cost to the subspace with least uncertainty improves planning performance significantly. This method achieved gains up to $+54.7$ points on 2D navigation tasks.

items.title: Quadratic Sample Complexity for Strictly Replicable Realizable Learning with Unknown Marginals
items.summary: The paper determines the sample-complexity exponent for strict replicability when the realizable distribution and its marginal are unknown. It establishes that two independent samples and one shared seed must yield identical functions for strict replicability. For specific parameters, the worst-case sample complexity is shown to be $\Theta((\log M)^2)$ without iterated logarithms. Furthermore, the work provides a matching characterization $\Theta(d^2/(\varepsilon\rho^2)+\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta))$ for the full Boolean class $P_d$ using a proper Poissonized ball-sampling algorithm. The results involve lower bounds using square-root probabilities and volumetric packing, and an explicit Gibbs upper bound.

items.title: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
items.summary: Continuum-LM introduces a continuous-depth language model by treating pretrained residual transformations as dynamical operators. Hidden states evolve via ordinary differential equations solved by higher-order numerical integration, with solver settings controlling the computation. This approach allows for extending computational depth by reusing parameters beyond simple model scaling. Experiments across eight scientific tasks show Continuum-LM achieves significant accuracy improvements over discrete models. The results suggest that continuous hidden-state evolution is a practical dimension for scientific language models.

items.title: Diffusion Score Estimation with Shallow Neural Networks: Regularity, Approximation, and Finite-Sample Rates
items.summary: The study investigates the sample complexity for estimating Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusion scores using denoising score matching with shallow ReLU networks. It derives explicit Sobolev bounds by combining estimates from the Gaussian transition kernel and the initial density, which control approximation error and path-norm budgets. The work establishes high-probability risk bounds for empirical score minimizers using truncation and localized Rademacher complexity. Under specific assumptions, the resulting squared $L^2(P_t)$ score risk is $\widetilde O(n^{-(d+3)/(2d+3)})$. Furthermore, aggregating errors leads to a total-variation error bound of $\widetilde O(n^{-(d+3)/(4d+6)})$ for generated versus original data distributions.

items.title: Communication Complexity of Universal Features
items.summary: The paper studies the communication complexity of representing data that allows for evaluation with a family of functions. It constructs a deterministic encoder that outputs a representation of size $O(d^{*}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits for a task $f$ with error $\varepsilon$. The encoder greedily selects functions based on a novel potential function argument comparing entropy gain to pattern count. The lower bounds show the representation length is worst-case optimal for $d^* \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon < 1/4$. The work also provides methods to learn this representation from unlabeled samples with guarantees on size and sample complexity.

items.title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits
items.summary: The research focuses on robust estimation of a Gaussian precision matrix that has a sparse component minus a low-rank component, arising from latent variable marginalization. A proposed convex estimator uses a centered Gaussian measure-transformed covariance and penalizes the low-rank part using the nuclear norm. A primal-dual witness theorem guarantees that the raw optimizer is unique and recovers the true structure under certain conditions. The work establishes information-theoretic limits for estimating inertia and signed graphs, providing specific sample complexity bounds. Finally, robustness to Huber contamination is quantified, showing vanishing bias for remote outliers under the MT functional.

items.title: Transformers Learn Two Competing Sorting Algorithms, and Only One Length-Generalizes
items.summary: Two-layer transformers trained on a sorting task converge to one of two solution classes based on initialization. One class fails to length-generalize, while the other perfectly length-generalizes despite fixed-length training. This difference in generalization stems from how the attention layers interact with input types that become more common at longer sequences. The second class utilizes a mechanism where the second layer leverages contextual information from the first layer to narrow its search space. This research identifies a layer-wise specialization mechanism that allows the second attention layer to handle rare sequences effectively.

items.title: High-dimensional layer-state trajectories reveal the internal dynamics of transformer inference
items.summary: Mechanistic studies of large language models focus on parameters but lack insight into the inference unfolding process. The ordered layer-state trajectory is examined to determine if layer order corresponds to a measurable computation during inference. Empirical results show that layer order aligns with endpoint-preserving shuffles in transformer checkpoints. Direct hidden states offer stronger mechanism coordinates than vocabulary readbacks for this process. Ultimately, layer order reveals an observable and computable aspect of transformer inference without a full theory of LLM dynamics.

items.title: CorteXforge: Scenario-Based RF Dataset Generation on Real Testbeds
items.summary: CorteXforge is a framework designed to generate realistic and reproducible Radio Frequency (RF) datasets using programmable Software Defined Radio (SDR) testbeds. It automatically translates high-level RF scenarios into synchronized experiments on platforms like SLICES-RI/CorteXlab. This process produces fully annotated Signal Metadata Format (SIGMF) datasets that include hardware impairments and propagation effects. Validation involved automatic modulation classification using an over-the-air (OTA) dataset generated by the framework. The work demonstrates that synthetic pretraining is beneficial for adapting to real-world OTA data, offering a foundation for reproducible RF data generation.

items.title: Ask to Learn: Query-Based Collaborative Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Offline reinforcement learning is limited by data coverage, prompting the study of methods to acquire information without direct environment interaction. Query-based collaborative reinforcement learning introduces a method where a learner queries a collaborator who samples actions based on a fixed policy. This approach is used to efficiently obtain complementary information from the offline dataset for tasks like collaborator-mediated simulation. For finite-horizon problems, the work derives information-theoretic lower bounds and develops an adaptive query-allocation algorithm. Experiments confirm the empirical efficiency of this method across various synthetic and semi-synthetic environments.

items.title: Bayesian Neural Networks via Dirichlet Process Priors on the Data-Generating Distribution for Randomized Value Functions in Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Bayesian neural networks are introduced to quantify epistemic uncertainty, addressing limitations of standard weight-space priors in deep reinforcement learning. The method places Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet Process priors directly on the data-generating distribution instead of network parameters. This leads to the development of DP-DQN, a reinforcement learning algorithm that uses these DP-BNNs for value function uncertainty. DP-DQN combines data-driven reweighting with generative prior hypotheses for deep exploration. This approach avoids the computational cost of multi-network ensembles.

items.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: MAMath-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning of multi-agent systems. It assesses systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial perturbations. The benchmark includes 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories and modalities like text, images, and audio. Evaluation findings indicate that multi-agent collaboration does not always improve final accuracy but can enhance reasoning coverage. Furthermore, current systems remain vulnerable to errors caused by subtle structural perturbations.

items.title: Gaussian Approximation of Besov Functions for Logistic Classification on Manifolds
items.summary: The study investigates using Gaussian kernel approximation and regularized logistic classification on smooth, connected, compact, embedded manifolds. The research addresses deriving a fast oracle inequality and constructing Gaussian approximants that leverage intrinsic dimension and regularity. A uniform Sobolev operator expansion is used, and Gaussian kernel integral operators are employed to cancel lower-order bias terms. This method yields an $L_2(X)$ approximation error of order $\gamma^\alpha$ and a squared Gaussian RKHS norm bound of order $\gamma^{-\varrho}$. The results establish bounds on the logistic excess-risk rate, which match the minimax optimal rate under certain conditions.

items.title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
items.summary: ORBIT is a unified deep generative framework designed for autoregressive time series generation by addressing challenges in learning hierarchical representations and coordinating heterogeneous temporal dynamics. It introduces two key components: the Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE for learning hierarchical representations and the Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer for autoregressive prediction. The framework uses these components to decompose temporal representations into frequency bands and establish a low-to-high frequency autoregressive direction. This approach disentangles patterns and mitigates interference between different temporal dynamics during generation. Experiments show ORBIT achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior inference efficiency.
